Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: Responsibility attaches to the Product Provider even where another actor performs the function. Assessment must cover each specified subject across the arrangement and relevant period; an outsourcing contract or successful operational snapshot cannot establish that coverage. Outsourcing is neither a prerequisite nor an exception. Footnote 1's illustrative reference to section 6.8 does not restrict the rule to that type of outsourcing.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

Prior consultation is also required for tokenisation of existing SFC-authorised investment products and/or material changes to the tokenisation arrangements of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. Such change(s) may require prior approval8.

8 For example, prior approval should be obtained before adding the disclosure of new tokenised unit/share class of an SFC-authorised fund in the Hong Kong offering documents and offering it to the public in Hong Kong. No prior approval is required for adding another tokenised unit/share class to the same fund if the tokenisation arrangement is substantially the same as the existing one.

original_reading.distinction: Retains the parent's allocation-focused reading after testing exception attachment. Outsourcing is expressly denied exculpatory effect across all three subjects. Footnote 1's applicability qualification concerns Appendix factors; section 6.8 is illustrative. Footnote 8's approval exception cannot migrate into paragraph 10. A delegate's failure may violate another safeguard without proving relinquishment of accountability. The strongest uncertainty is whether retained accountability, even with adequate oversight, can satisfy paragraph 10 when operational soundness or proper records fail. Mere contractual acceptance is not established as sufficient.

citations.quote: Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

Prior consultation is also required for tokenisation of existing SFC-authorised investment products and/or material changes to the tokenisation arrangements of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. Such change(s) may require prior approval8.

8 For example, prior approval should be obtained before adding the disclosure of new tokenised unit/share class of an SFC-authorised fund in the Hong Kong offering documents and offering it to the public in Hong Kong. No prior approval is required for adding another tokenised unit/share class to the same fund if the tokenisation arrangement is substantially the same as the existing one.

original_reading.distinction: Retains the parent's allocation-focused reading after testing exception attachment. Outsourcing is expressly denied exculpatory effect across all three subjects. Footnote 1's applicability qualification concerns Appendix factors; section 6.8 is illustrative. Footnote 8's approval exception cannot migrate into paragraph 10. A delegate's failure may violate another safeguard without proving relinquishment of accountability. The strongest uncertainty is whether retained accountability, even with adequate oversight, can satisfy paragraph 10 when operational soundness or proper records fail. Mere contractual acceptance is not established as sufficient.

original_reading.distinction: This reading treats paragraph 10 primarily as allocating non-transferable accountability. original_reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Under this proposed reading, the selected paragraph 10 control is satisfied when the Product Provider continues to bear ultimate accountability for management and operational soundness of its adopted tokenisation arrangement and ownership record keeping, including accountability for outsourced work. Performance may be allocated to service providers where otherwise permitted, but responsibility cannot be transferred or disclaimed through that allocation. True would mean this retained-accountability control is satisfied; false would mean it is not. Neither outcome decides compliance with the circular as a whole. The qualitative discharge standard is unresolved, so no executable test is proposed.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.

Tokenisation of investment products refers to the creation of blockchain-based tokens that represent or aim to represent ownership in an investment product. The tokenised product can then be recorded digitally on the blockchain, offered directly to end-investors, distributed by SFC-licensed intermediaries, or traded among the blockchain participants where allowed.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.

Tokenisation of investment products refers to the creation of blockchain-based tokens that represent or aim to represent ownership in an investment product. The tokenised product can then be recorded digitally on the blockchain, offered directly to end-investors, distributed by SFC-licensed intermediaries, or traded among the blockchain participants where allowed.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: The entity performing a function can differ from the entity retaining ultimate responsibility. Outsourcing does not create an exception or an antecedent to paragraph 10. Keeping the three responsibility components separate exposes partial transfers that a single responsibility Boolean would hide.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
2 Product Providers are not expected to issue tokenised SFC-authorised investment products in bearer form.
(a)      the tokenisation arrangement6, particularly, with clear disclosure on whether off-chain or on-chain settlement is final;
(b)      the ownership representation of the tokens (eg, legal and beneficial title of the tokens, ownership of / interests in the product); and

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

The packet supplies no threshold for failures, reasonable care, remediation or strict liability; it therefore does not justify treating every incident as an automatic breach.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: A materially stronger reading treats responsibility for management, operational soundness and records as requiring effective discharge as well as non-transferable accountability. Proper-records and assurance provisions support, but do not conclusively establish, this interpretation. Thus an outsourced failure could reveal a paragraph 10 deficiency even where accountability was never disclaimed. Both readings reject the same outsourcing-exemption hypothesis; the genuine rivalry concerns the content of responsibility, not an invented exception. The strongest uncertainty is the threshold for substantive failure: the source does not make every incident an automatic breach or impose an absolute guarantee.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

original_reading.distinction: This reading treats paragraph 10 principally as allocating continuing responsibility, with concrete performance duties stated separately. Consider an outsourced registrar whose failure makes ownership records materially unreliable, although the Product Provider retained effective supervision, intervention capacity and accountability and promptly undertook remediation. That failure does not alone establish breach of paragraph 10 under this reading; the separate records duty may nevertheless be breached. Under r2, an established failure of proper record keeping also defeats the selected paragraph 10 control. Neither reading permits responsibility to be transferred to the registrar.
questions: Does effective retained governance suffice for paragraph 10 when a separate performance requirement has failed?
Which powers, information rights, staffing and intervention arrangements establish effective responsibility without requiring the Product Provider to perform every task?
original_reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For the selected paragraph 10 responsibility control only, the Product Provider satisfies the requirement by retaining effective ultimate governance and accountability for management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping throughout outsourcing. Performance may be delegated; responsibility cannot. True would mean this retained-responsibility control is satisfied, while false would mean responsibility was displaced or was not effectively retained. An operational failure is relevant evidence but is not, by itself, conclusive of failure of this particular control. Footnote 1 reinforces this allocation across outsourcing arrangements; its conditional external reference does not qualify that allocation.

Possession of powers alone and achieved operational success alone do not establish this fact.
facts.unit: management conduct across the same adopted arrangement and period

facts.name: operational_stewardship_adequate
facts.meaning: Throughout that period, the provider actually exercises supervision, risk management and corrective responsibility for operational soundness to the independently established conduct standard, including outsourced operations and relevant interfaces. Incidents and recovery are assessed under that standard rather than automatically determining this fact.
facts.unit: operational stewardship across the same adopted arrangement and period

facts.name: recordkeeping_stewardship_adequate
facts.meaning: Throughout that period, the provider actually exercises supervision and corrective responsibility over all relevant ownership-record processes to the independently established conduct standard, including contractor records and record transfers. Actual record adequacy is evidence but is not an independent outcome conjunct under this proposed conduct reading.
facts.unit: ownership-record stewardship for the same product–arrangement–period

original_reading.subject: Effective exercise of responsibility distinguished from guaranteed substantive adequacy
original_reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Under this competing proposal, the selected paragraph 10 control requires continuing ultimate accountability together with effective exercise of management and supervisory responsibility for operation and ownership records, including outsourced functions. True means both requirements meet the applicable conduct standard; false means at least one fails. Actual deficiencies are relevant evidence but are not automatically dispositive. The conduct standard remains unresolved, so no executable test or overall-compliance conclusion is proposed.
original_reading.distinction: This preserves and sharpens the effective-exercise rivals already supplied. It distinguishes retained accountability, effective supervisory conduct and achieved adequacy. Effective conduct could satisfy this proposed reading despite an incident that establishes inadequate records under a separate outcome requirement; nominal accountability without effective supervision could fail it. The source does not conclusively select this intermediate reading.

A performance defect is relevant evidence but does not alone establish that this selected accountability requirement failed. No executable compliance test follows until effective accountability is defined.
original_reading.distinction: Preserves the allocation rival already represented in the retained candidates. An established records defect can defeat the substantive conjunction while leaving effective retained accountability intact. Whether that distinction determines paragraph 10 compliance remains unresolved.

original_reading.subject: Effective stewardship as distinct from retained allocation and guaranteed outcomes
original_reading.statement: Under this competing proposal, paragraph 10 requires continuing accountability together with effective exercise of management, supervision and corrective responsibility across the adopted arrangement and ownership records. True would mean that this conduct-based responsibility standard is satisfied; false would mean it is not. Actual failures are relevant evidence, but neither contractual acceptance nor an incident alone determines satisfaction. Undefined conduct and temporal standards prevent executable formalization.
original_reading.distinction: Preserves the existing effective-exercise rivals while distinguishing a conduct standard from an achieved-outcome standard. A provider accepting accountability but lacking effective supervision could fail; a supervised contractor's remediable incident would not automatically decide the result. The supplied text does not settle either threshold.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: Responsibility attaches to the Product Provider even where another actor performs the function. Assessment must cover each specified subject across the arrangement and relevant period; an outsourcing contract or successful operational snapshot cannot establish that coverage. Outsourcing is neither a prerequisite nor an exception. Footnote 1's illustrative reference to section 6.8 does not restrict the rule to that type of outsourcing.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

In the outsourced-registrar case in r1, established material unreliability defeats this selected control despite effective oversight and acceptance of responsibility. Its strongest uncertainty is whether that conclusion imports separate performance duties into paragraph 10, whose immediate language focuses on who remains responsible. Neither the incident threshold nor any strict-liability consequence is supplied.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: This reading gives substantive effect to responsibility for soundness and records, strengthened by footnote 1's investor-ownership rationale and the later requirement to confirm and demonstrate soundness. In the outsourced-registrar case in r1, established material unreliability defeats this selected control despite effective oversight and acceptance of responsibility. Its strongest uncertainty is whether that conclusion imports separate performance duties into paragraph 10, whose immediate language focuses on who remains responsible. Neither the incident threshold nor any strict-liability consequence is supplied.

Outsourcing and diligent supervision do not by themselves cure an established failure in those domains. citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.

Tokenisation of investment products refers to the creation of blockchain-based tokens that represent or aim to represent ownership in an investment product. The tokenised product can then be recorded digitally on the blockchain, offered directly to end-investors, distributed by SFC-licensed intermediaries, or traded among the blockchain participants where allowed.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: The entity performing a function can differ from the entity retaining ultimate responsibility. Outsourcing does not create an exception or an antecedent to paragraph 10. citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.

Tokenisation of investment products refers to the creation of blockchain-based tokens that represent or aim to represent ownership in an investment product. The tokenised product can then be recorded digitally on the blockchain, offered directly to end-investors, distributed by SFC-licensed intermediaries, or traded among the blockchain participants where allowed.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: Separate the identity of the accountable Product Provider from the identity of the performer. Outsourcing changes who performs a function without relieving the Product Provider of responsibility for management, operational soundness or ownership record keeping. Footnote 1 reinforces this across outsourcing arrangements; its reference to section 6.8 is illustrative, and its applicability qualification concerns the referenced factors.

citations.quote: Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

Prior consultation is also required for tokenisation of existing SFC-authorised investment products and/or material changes to the tokenisation arrangements of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. Such change(s) may require prior approval8.

8 For example, prior approval should be obtained before adding the disclosure of new tokenised unit/share class of an SFC-authorised fund in the Hong Kong offering documents and offering it to the public in Hong Kong. No prior approval is required for adding another tokenised unit/share class to the same fund if the tokenisation arrangement is substantially the same as the existing one.

Prior consultation is also required for tokenisation of existing SFC-authorised investment products and/or material changes to the tokenisation arrangements of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. Such change(s) may require prior approval8.

8 For example, prior approval should be obtained before adding the disclosure of new tokenised unit/share class of an SFC-authorised fund in the Hong Kong offering documents and offering it to the public in Hong Kong. No prior approval is required for adding another tokenised unit/share class to the same fund if the tokenisation arrangement is substantially the same as the existing one.

original_reading.subject: Effective exercise of responsibility distinguished from guaranteed substantive adequacy

True means both requirements meet the applicable conduct standard; false means at least one fails. Actual deficiencies are relevant evidence but are not automatically dispositive. original_reading.distinction: This preserves and sharpens the effective-exercise rivals already supplied. 1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: A materially stronger reading treats responsibility for management, operational soundness and records as requiring effective discharge as well as non-transferable accountability. Proper-records and assurance provisions support, but do not conclusively establish, this interpretation. Thus an outsourced failure could reveal a paragraph 10 deficiency even where accountability was never disclaimed. Both readings reject the same outsourcing-exemption hypothesis; the genuine rivalry concerns the content of responsibility, not an invented exception. The strongest uncertainty is the threshold for substantive failure: the source does not make every incident an automatic breach or impose an absolute guarantee.

original_reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Under this competing proposal, true means the Product Provider both retains ultimate accountability and effectively discharges responsibility for management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping under the applicable substantive standard; false means that selected paragraph 10 requirement is not satisfied. This responsibility includes outsourced functions. Appendix applicability and the additional-class approval exception do not qualify it. Personal execution of every function is not required by this interpretation, and strict liability is not inferred. The source uses SHOULD, and the substantive standard is unresolved; no executable test or actual truth value is proposed.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
2 Product Providers are not expected to issue tokenised SFC-authorised investment products in bearer form.
(a)      the tokenisation arrangement6, particularly, with clear disclosure on whether off-chain or on-chain settlement is final;
(b)      the ownership representation of the tokens (eg, legal and beneficial title of the tokens, ownership of / interests in the product); and

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: The prior allocation predicate could be satisfied while the provider cannot supervise outsourced components or ownership records fail at service-provider interfaces. citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

original_reading.distinction: This reading gives paragraph 10 substantive assurance content beyond allocation of accountability. A provider that remains the accountable entity but has not secured the required operational soundness or proper records could fail this selected control. The records duty and confirmation/demonstration provisions support that reading, but may instead be separate duties supporting r1. The packet supplies no threshold for failures, reasonable care, remediation or strict liability; it therefore does not justify treating every incident as an automatic breach.
questions: Does full responsibility impose an affirmative assurance standard within paragraph 10, and what standard measures its discharge?
How do deficiencies, remedial action and outsourced-provider failures affect that standard without assuming an absolute guarantee?
original_reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Under this proposed reading, the selected paragraph 10 control requires the Product Provider both to retain ultimate accountability and to discharge an affirmative responsibility to secure sound management and operation of the adopted tokenisation arrangement and proper ownership record keeping. Outsourcing cannot reduce that responsibility, although permitted service providers may perform the work. True would mean this substantive responsibility has been discharged under the applicable standard; false would mean it has not. This is neither a personal-performance requirement nor a finding of strict liability or whole-circular compliance. Because the applicable assurance standard is missing, no executable test is proposed.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

original_reading.distinction: This reading treats paragraph 10 principally as allocating continuing responsibility, with concrete performance duties stated separately. Consider an outsourced registrar whose failure makes ownership records materially unreliable, although the Product Provider retained effective supervision, intervention capacity and accountability and promptly undertook remediation. That failure does not alone establish breach of paragraph 10 under this reading; the separate records duty may nevertheless be breached. Under r2, an established failure of proper record keeping also defeats the selected paragraph 10 control. Neither reading permits responsibility to be transferred to the registrar.

original_reading.subject: Effective stewardship as distinct from retained allocation and guaranteed outcomes
original_reading.statement: Under this competing proposal, paragraph 10 requires continuing accountability together with effective exercise of management, supervision and corrective responsibility across the adopted arrangement and ownership records. True would mean that this conduct-based responsibility standard is satisfied; false would mean it is not. Actual failures are relevant evidence, but neither contractual acceptance nor an incident alone determines satisfaction. Undefined conduct and temporal standards prevent executable formalization.
original_reading.distinction: Preserves the existing effective-exercise rivals while distinguishing a conduct standard from an achieved-outcome standard.
